data.description:

They previously made an even bigger sale of -AU$593k worth of shares at a price of AU$11.85 per share. So it's clear an insider wanted to take some cash off the table, even below the current price of AU$13.05. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. data.title: 3 Infrastructure Stocks That Could Benefit From Spending Moving Outside Saudi Arabia
data.description:
Geopolitical risk around Saudi infrastructure is suddenly front and center, with drone strikes, weaker IMF forecasts, and possible cuts to megaproject spending forcing capital to reconsider where it feels safest. That shift can hurt some businesses yet open doors for others as money looks for infrastructure and construction exposure outside the kingdom. This article walks through 3 stocks exposed to that story and explains why each may warrant a closer look today.

The three stocks highlighted below are only a starting sample. The full screen surfaced 46 more infrastructure and construction companies with equally compelling narratives that are not covered in this article.

ACS Actividades de Construcción y Servicios (BME:ACS)

Overview: ACS Actividades de Construcción y Servicios is a Madrid based infrastructure group that builds and operates large transport, energy and digital projects across Europe and the Americas, offering investors broad exposure to capital spending that may shift away from Saudi focused megaprojects.

Operations: ACS generates about €29.4b from Turner, €11.2b from Engineering and Construction, €10.9b from Cimic and €2.6b from HQ and non core activities, anchored by sizeable exposure to the United States, Australia and Spain.

Market Cap: €21.6b

ACS Actividades de Construcción y Servicios matters for this theme because its construction and concessions portfolio is tied to long duration infrastructure programs in Europe and the Americas. The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St treats the company as a key beneficiary if capital reallocates away from Saudi focused megaprojects.

"The shift toward owning and operating capital intensive platforms, such as data center campuses through Coravel and Waterford alongside extended road concessions at Abertis, gives ACS Actividades de Construcción y Servicios a path to increase recurring EBITDA and net profit contribution from contracted capacity and toll like revenue rather than one off construction margins."

What happens if a single assumption about how quickly that long dated backlog turns into high margin recurring income proves too cautious?

If that shift unfolds faster than expected, read the full narrative for ACS Actividades de Construcción y Servicios to see how ACS Actividades de Construcción y Servicios could convert it into accelerating contracted earnings power.

Worley (ASX:WOR)

Overview: Worley is a global engineering and project delivery group that designs, builds and manages energy, chemicals and resources infrastructure across major regions. This positions the business to capture Gulf capital that may flow into complex projects outside Saudi Arabia.

Operations: Worley generates about A$6.2b of revenue from the Americas, A$4.5b from EMEA and A$1.3b from APAC, plus smaller unallocated items.

Market Cap: A$5.0b

Worley matters for this screener theme because its engineering bench is already embedded in large energy and industrial projects worldwide. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St therefore focuses on how any shift in where capital is deployed could reshape its project mix and earnings profile.

Any continuation or worsening of disruptions tied to delayed project awards from the Middle East conflict would limit revenue growth and weigh on earnings."

What happens to Worley’s future earnings power hinges on how one pressure point reshapes the balance between higher value projects and delayed awards.

HOCHTIEF (XTRA:HOT)

Operations: HOCHTIEF generates most of its revenue from the Turner segment at about €29.4b and CIMIC at about €10.9b, with around €1.8b from Engineering and Construction in Europe and Flatiron Dragados.
